Are you paying for subscriptions you forgot about? 💸

Here's how to find ALL your recurring charges, including the hidden places you might not think to check.

Get everything in one list, then cancel the subscriptions you no longer use. You could save hundreds of dollars a year!

💬 Comment CHECK and I'll send you my step-by-step guide to finding and canceling forgotten subscriptions.

#RichOnTech #TechTips #SaveMoney

media.transcript: Rich DeMuro here, Rich on Tech, with another quick tip. It is so easy to sign up for subscriptions these days, you might forget what you're paying for or to cancel before that free trial ends. So here's how to figure out what you're paying for and how to cancel what you don't need. First, check your credit card statements. Look for recurring charges, and don't forget annual subscriptions. Some banking apps will even show you a list of recurring payments. Next, check Apple and Google. On iPhone, open the settings, tap your name, then subscriptions. On Android, open Google Play, tap your profile picture, then payments and subscriptions, then tap subscriptions. Cancel anything you no longer use. And don't forget, subscriptions can also be billed through Amazon, PayPal, and Roku, so be sure to check there too. If you want some help finding all your subscriptions, there are apps for that. Rocket Money can find and list your recurring subscriptions for free. If you want help cancelling them, that's a paid upgrade. ChatGBT has a finances feature that lets you connect your accounts, see recurring charges, and figure out which subscriptions are worth keeping. And Meta's Muse AI Assistant can also help you find and even cancel subscriptions if you connect your financial accounts. Just remember, connecting your financial accounts means you might be sharing some sensitive information, so check the access you're granting before you say yes. Another trick, search your email for words like subscription, renewal, or free trial. You might find something you forgot about. And remember, deleting an app does not cancel its subscription. My favorite tip of all, when you sign up for a free trial, you can usually cancel it right away and still use it until that free trial ends. Many services let you do this, but not all. Some, like Apple, might end your access immediately. If that's the case, set a calendar reminder or snooze that confirmation email until a few days before the trial expires. That way, you can decide whether it's worth paying for instead of getting charged because you forgot. Finding just two or three subscriptions you don't need or use could save you hundreds of dollars a year.

I built a personal subscription tracker with Replit + Plaid to get my spending subscriptions under control.

Here’s how you can build one yourself:

1️⃣ Connect your financial data: In Replit, find Plaid connector to securely retrieve transactions for the past 2 years. It’s very easy to set up and super useful!

2️⃣ Build with Replit: Ask Replit Agent to pull transactions, identify recurring subscriptions, and build an interface so you can review and adjust them.

3️⃣ Visualize your spending: Ask it to create a dashboard showing monthly costs, spending trends, and active subscriptions.

That’s it! Now you can see what you’re still paying for but no longer use.

💡 Pro tip: Claude now has Replit connector. I found it much easier asking Claude to build in Replit than prompting myself.

Which subscriptions do you find most useful, and which ones are you planning to cancel? Why?

Let me know in the comments!

🔗 If you to build your own app try Replit for free. Use my referral link in bio to get $10 in credits.

______
P.S. This is part 1 of 3 of my journey to get my finances under control. Follow for the next video 2 where I show how to extend this app to a personal finance management.

#AITools #ReplitPartner #Claude #LearnAI #Finance

media.transcript: Let me show you how much I spend on AI subscriptions. I automate most of my work with AI. So to keep track of all my subscriptions, I've decided to build an app in Replit. Let me show you how I did it so you can do the same. So first, we need to pull financial transactions. You have two choices. You can either upload your statements or utilize plate connector to pull them directly. So in Replit first, I added the plate connector and then I asked to build an app. The agent connected to my credit cards, pulled two years of history, and then saved all those transactions into a database. Then it built the classification logic to identify which ones are actually subscriptions. Once this is done, you can also review and adjust them. As you can see, my overall spend has been increasing. This month I spent $284. From this, $160 is called. But the good thing is that I canceled also a few subscriptions like Courser and Figma because I switched this design and coding work now to Claude. So now that I have this app, I can monitor and analyze my monthly charges across all my credit cards. If you want to build this app yourself, find the steps in the description and follow for more practical AI tips.

media.transcript: GTA 6 cuesta $100 pesos en México. Ya ves, Bibi, esas sí son ofertas. Aunque no te lo creas, al parecer el nuevo GTA está a un precio de $100 pesos en la PlayStation Store. Pero antes de que te vuelvas loco, esto se trata de un simple error. Pues si no sabías, PlayStation está llevando a cabo una actualización en su tienda ya que por fin pondrán precios regionales en México. Y es que desde hace unas horas varios usuarios de Play han estado aportando que en la tienda digital los juegos ya salen en precios mexicanos. Presumiendo que hay muchos juegos y suscripciones a precios regalados. Lo peor de todo es que muchos aprovechados quieren comprar e incluso demandar con Profeco por estos bugs de precios. Por obvias razones ninguna de estas compras se pueden finalizar e incluso PlayStation ya había avisado que la tienda estaría en mantenimiento. Y la verdad no es por defender a Play. Pero no puedo creer que haya gente sin sentido común peleando por este tipo de precios. Pero en fin, todo apunta a que mañana ya sabremos si Play seguirá cobrando impuestos aparte al finalizar una compra. O al menos ya dejan de ser unos hambreados y de verdad ponen precios regionales que valgan la pena.
